question: how does micro-batch differ from true streaming
answer:
[Ch. 8] "Micro-batching is a way to take a batch-oriented framework and apply it in a streaming situation. A micro-batch might run anywhere from every two minutes to every second. Some micro-batch frameworks (e.g., Apache Spark Streaming) are designed for this use case and will perform well with appropriately allocated resources at a high batch frequency. (In truth, DBAs and engineers have long used micro-batching with more traditional databases; this often led to horrific performance and resource consumption.)"
Micro-batching lets you use batch processing for streaming data, from every two minutes to every second.
checker_note: answers the difference; gloss tight
